subject.title: Feature request: Read pinned Telegram messages via bot API

question: Should OpenClaw expose Telegram pinned-message reads, and should the first version be an explicit on-demand gated action/command rather than automatic session context?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but this feature decides how persistent Telegram chat content is authorized, exposed to agents, and possibly injected into session context.

options.title: On-demand gated action first
options.body: Add a Telegram-owned read-pinned/list-pins action or native command backed by getChat.pinned_message, disabled by a clear action/config gate and proven with live Telegram evidence.

options.title: Fold into broader Telegram read design
options.body: Track pinned reads under the broader Telegram message-read work at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12756 and settle retention/history semantics before implementation.

options.title: Defer automatic context injection
options.body: Do not add session-start pinned context until maintainers approve an explicit storage, privacy, and prompt-injection policy.

recommendation.title: On-demand gated action first
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram-owned read-pinned/list-pins action or native command backed by getChat.pinned_message, disabled by a clear action/config gate and proven with live Telegram evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The previous review already routed the product/security decision here, and this is primarily a maintainer policy choice rather than a mechanical code fix.
